candidate_relations.reason: CT showed luminal patency, so small-bowel obstruction is not the inflammatory jejunal process.
Mesenteric panniculitis is a primary mesenteric inflammatory disease, not diverticulitis of the jejunum.
There is no chronic enteritis pattern or endoscopic Crohn disease; this is an acute jejunal diverticular inflammation.
Diverticulitis is the correct family but omits the jejunal site required by the reference.
Epidemic diverticulitis is not a recognized entity matching this isolated jejunal diverticulitis.
Gastrointestinal lymphoma is a neoplastic differential for bowel-wall thickening, not diverticulitis.
Small-bowel lymphoma is a different neoplastic diagnosis.
Gastroenteritis does not produce focal jejunal wall thickening with mesenteric edema 25 cm beyond Treitz.
Eosinophilic gastroenteritis is an allergic mucosal disease not supported here.
Inflammatory bowel disease is a chronic idiopathic colitis/enteritis, not jejunal diverticulitis.
Duodenal diverticula were noted, but the inflammatory focus is jejunal, not a duodenal ulcer.
Mesenteric lymphadenopathy is a reactive imaging accompaniment of the diverticulitis, not the diagnosis.

case_quality_flags: No candidate specifies jejunal diverticulitis; CT localized inflammation 25 cm beyond the ligament of Treitz.
